headline: Kyiv Again Records Zero Missile Intercepts
deck: Four days after this paper reported an empty Patriot magazine, another mass-casualty barrage left 17 dead and 44 injured. Ukraine said it neutralised 98 drones while intercepting none of 28 missiles.
body: Ukraine’s Air Force said it neutralised 98 drones during the 5 August barrage but intercepted none of 28 incoming missiles [E1][E3]. The missile inventory comprised four Zircon or Oniks missiles and 24 ballistic missiles, alongside 115 UAVs [E3]. Ukrainian authorities reported 17 people killed and 44 injured in Kyiv and the surrounding region [E1][E2]. The official tally therefore records a mass-casualty night with a complete missile-interception failure [E1][E3].

Four days after this paper’s 2 August report of an empty Patriot magazine, the Air Force published another zero for missile interceptions [E3]. The 5 August record concerns a separate barrage, with a fresh casualty count and its own full inventory of incoming weapons [E1][E3]. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said interceptors could have saved lives [E4]. His claim is a counterfactual, but the engagement count gives it a concrete premise: none of the 28 missiles was reported intercepted [E3][E4].

Drone defence and missile defence split cleanly in the official count [E3]. Ukrainian forces neutralised 98 of 115 UAVs while reporting zero interceptions across all 28 missiles [E3]. Any combined interception total would blur that gap, because success against drones produced no recorded missile intercept [E3]. The night exposed a categorical failure: one threat class was heavily reduced, while the other recorded no interceptions [E3].

Impacts reached commercial warehouses, a Nova Poshta postal sorting centre and a railway station [E2]. Those locations put civilian movement and supply infrastructure inside the same casualty story [E2]. Nova Poshta said cluster munitions were used against its facility, a claim carried as the company’s statement [E2]. The cluster-munition description remains attributed to Nova Poshta, not presented as an independently established finding [E2].

Damage to warehouses, a sorting centre and a railway station does not by itself establish what Russian planners intended to hit [E2]. The available record establishes the struck locations and the casualty toll, while Russian targeting intent remains contested [E1][E2]. Logistical consequences can be documented without converting impact sites into proof of motive [E2]. The damage pattern is established, while the intent behind it remains unresolved [E2].

Seventeen deaths and 44 injuries set the scale of the human loss [E1][E2][E4]. The railway station and postal facility show how the same barrage also struck systems built to move people and goods [E2]. Zelenskyy linked the toll to the absence of successful missile interceptions, saying interceptors could have saved lives [E3][E4]. The official numbers cannot prove each counterfactual life saved, but they show that the night ended with no reported missile intercepts [E3][E4].

The continuity from 2 August is numerical before it is rhetorical. A previous report concerned an empty Patriot magazine; four days later, the Air Force again published zero missile interceptions for a major attack [E3]. This time the record also carried 17 dead, 44 injured and damage across commercial and transport sites [E1][E2]. The final missile line remained the sharpest fact in the barrage report: 28 incoming, zero intercepted [E3].

evidence_box.fragment: 17 people killed and 44 injured in Kyiv and Kyiv region
Nova Poshta said cluster munitions struck its sorting facility
Four Zircon or Oniks, 24 ballistic missiles and zero interceptions
17 deaths, 44 injuries; interceptors could have saved lives

art.caption: The strike crossed Kyiv and its western and eastern approaches; Ukraine reported no interceptions from the 28-missile package.
